title: fix(studio): live Stitch Detail study replaces stale Sienna treatment stills (V1)
body: ## Summary V1 of the approved visual plan. The Material step's treatment card showed a fixed Sienna Brown photograph per treatment, and the "Classic" photo showed perforated leather. The card now shows a **live study**: a close-up rendered by the existing viewer from the Stitch Detail camera, in the customer's current treatment, primary/secondary colours and thread. How it works: ``` TreatmentSlider (card on screen) ── setWanted(studyKey{treatment, primary, secondary, thread}) ──▶ treatmentStudyStore SpikeModel (existing canvas) ── if wanted === current key && no study for it: 600 ms debounce, then after the next frame: setSize(900 px card) → setViewOffset(Stitch Detail, lower-right region) → render → drawImage to a 2D canvas → restore size, clearViewOffset → re-render visible view → toBlob → publish({key, blob URL}) (old blob URL revoked) Card: studyState(snapshot, key) → "ready" | "updating" (previous image dimmed, "Rendering …") | "unavailable" (viewer error/empty, or capture produced no image) ``` - No new canvas, WebGL context or GLB download. One extra frame is rendered per change, and only while the card is mounted (so on step 1 only). The visible stage is redrawn in the same task, so it never shows the study frame. - A study is labelled current only when its key matches the selection. Otherwise the card says it is updating, so it can never present another treatment or colour as yours. - Card copy: caption `LIVE STUDY · ` and the note "Rendered from your live cabin. Physical samples at the studio determine the final material appearance." - Deleted `public/showroom/{classic,diamond,perforated}-seam_macro.png`. They had no other users; `welcome-cabin.png` (splash) is unchanged. - `stageColours()` is shared by the stage and the card, so both apply the same monotone/duotone colour rule. - Unchanged: step count, layout, Blender sources, GLBs, design tokens, treatment switching (click, keys, swipe), Retry/recovery, WhatsApp (still disabled). ### Before / after (production build, Chromium SwiftShader; B = `main` 9081e79, A = this branch) Desktop 1440×900, Sienna Brown / Exclusive Black (default Duotone): ![desktop sienna](/home/ubuntu/v1-work/pr/desktop-sienna-before-after.png) Desktop, Exclusive Black: ![desktop black](/home/ubuntu/v1-work/pr/desktop-black-before-after.png) Mobile 390×844, Sienna Brown: ![mobile sienna](/home/ubuntu/v1-work/pr/mobile-sienna-before-after.png) Mobile, Exclusive Black: ![mobile black](/home/ubuntu/v1-work/pr/mobile-black-before-after.png) Full page after (desktop, Perforated · Sienna): ![after desktop page](/home/ubuntu/v1-work/pr/after-desktop-page.png) ### Tests - `tests/treatment-study.test.ts` (new, 9 tests): key covers treatment and all three colours; a mismatched or failed study is never "ready"; the previous blob URL is revoked; the region stays in-frame at the card aspect; colour rule is shared; the stale stills and their copy are gone from `public/` and `src/`. - `e2e/smoke/studio.smoke.spec.ts` (+2, runs in CI): each treatment's study is a `blob:` image keyed to that treatment; the three studies differ pairwise by more than 3 % of pixels; changing to Sienna updates the key and the image gets redder; there is still one canvas, no `seam_macro.png` request and no console errors; on a 390 px phone the card fits and switching treatment works. Local results at a2cee48: typecheck pass; lint 0 errors (4 existing warnings); `npm test` 133/133; production build pass; smoke 6/6; front-cabin-runtime + lexus-runtime with `--repeat-each=2` 26/26 (same as `main`). Earlier full dev-server run at this design: 36 passed, 3 skipped by design; the 2 failures there were 5 s readiness polls, which is what the debounce fixed. An earlier draft captured on every material change at up to 3× buffer size, which made 11 dev-server E2E tests time out under SwiftShader. Capturing on demand at card size, debounced by 600 ms, fixed it. ### Risks / not verified - The capture cost is unmeasured on a hardware GPU and a physical phone. It is one stage-sized frame per selection change while step 1 is open. - Classic and Perforated read clearly apart at card size, but perforation in Exclusive Black is subtle. Human visual review is still needed; this PR makes no visual-acceptance claim. --- 🟢 Devin fixed the [finding](https://app.devin.ai/review/suyanka21/autolab-digital-showroom/pull/6) · [Follow Devin's work](https://app.devin.ai/sessions/17e0a6bb7b064d8ea31a23552f887937)

title: test(e2e): make the browser suite reliable and add a production smoke job to CI
body: ## Summary P0 PR 5 of 5. Before this PR, `npm run test:e2e` failed 14 of 48 tests. It also wrote screenshots and JSON into the committed `docs/review/` audit folders, and no browser test ran in CI. After this PR, the full suite passes locally (38 passed, 3 skipped by design), never writes to `docs/review/`, and a 4-test production smoke suite runs in CI. **Root causes and fixes** | Failure (assessment) | Root cause | Fix | |---|---|---| | 8 tests: `msedge` not found | `test.use({channel:'msedge'})` was hard-coded in 3 specs | `playwright.config.ts` reads `channel: process.env.TEST_BROWSER_CHANNEL \|\| undefined`, so it defaults to the bundled Chromium. The workshop PC can set `TEST_BROWSER_CHANNEL=msedge`. | | 6 + 1 stale assertions | `spike-viewer.spec.ts` targets the retired S-Class `spike.glb` presets, and `lexus-refinement.spec.ts` targets `driver-seat-l2a.glb`. The app loads neither. `quality.spec.ts` expected `immutable` on `/assets/3d/*`, which `next.config.ts` now deliberately serves `must-revalidate`. | Both superseded specs are retired; the GLB files and their historical evidence stay. The immutable check now targets `/draco/draco_decoder.wasm`, which is still immutable by design. | | Cache-upgrade test: canvas never appeared | The local caching proxy did not forward the dev server's `/_next/hmr` WebSocket (404 on handshake), so the proxied page never hydrated | The proxy forwards `upgrade` requests to the dev server over a raw TCP tunnel and destroys the tunnels in `finally`. The test assertions are unchanged. | | Runs rewrote `docs/review/` | Each spec's default evidence directory was a dated review folder | Defaults are now `test-results/evidence//`, which git ignores. The live-trim specs create that folder in `beforeAll`, so a single test can run on its own. The `*_EVIDENCE_DIR` overrides still work. Specs still **read** `docs/review/front-cabin-2026-11-05/evidence/assets.json` as the expected SHA list. | **Production smoke suite in CI** - `playwright.smoke.config.ts` runs `e2e/smoke/` against `next start` on port 3200; `npm run test:smoke` runs it after a build. - The main config skips the smoke folder (`testIgnore: "smoke/**"`). - New `e2e-smoke` job in `ci.yml`: install Chromium, build, run the smoke suite, and upload `test-results/` if it fails. - The four smoke tests: - the cabin GLB loads, one canvas, no viewer error or fallback, no `__autolab`, no console errors, all four camera tabs present; - Composition lists only Bespoke Monotone and Duotone; - WhatsApp booking is disabled; - `/dashboard` and `/auth` return 404, and `/splash` links back to a live canvas. **Docs** `docs/quality/testing-runbook.md` covers the commands, environment variables and output folders. It also records the Python gap: 3 of 18 Python tests error out on a clean clone because they read Blender outputs that git ignores (`blender/out/lexus-l4a/*.png`, `blender/out/lexus-l4ar1/atlas.json`). It proposes a focused follow-up PR, not implemented here: skip those tests with a reason when the outputs are absent, enforce them with `AUTOLAB_REQUIRE_BLENDER_OUT=1`, and run the source-only Python tests in CI with pinned `numpy`/`Pillow`. **Verification (local, Node 22.23.2, SwiftShader)** | Check | Result | |---|---| | Clean clone: `npm ci`, typecheck, build | exit 0 | | Clean clone: lint | 0 errors (4 existing warnings) | | Clean clone: `npm test` | 124/124 | | Clean clone: `npm run test:smoke` | 4/4 passed | | Full `npm run test:e2e` (after merging `main` with PR #4) | 38 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed (10.2 min) | | `git status` after the full run | clean: nothing written under `docs/review/` | | Single `inspect dashboard trim` test with no `test-results/` folder | passed | | GitHub Actions `checks` and `e2e-smoke` | passed | The 3 skipped specs need `PRODUCTION_NO_PROBE=1` against a production server, as before. The full suite stays local-only: it takes about 10 minutes with software WebGL. title: fix(studio): open on a reframed Driver Hero so seat colour is visible
body: ## Summary P0 PR 4 of 5. The Studio now opens on a view where the selected seat colour is visible. It also fixes the grey foreground mass in Driver Hero by reframing the camera only; no model was changed. **Problem** 1. **Opening view:** the Studio opened on Cabin Pair, which looks forward from behind the front seats. The seat backs do not take the primary colour. Measured: switching Exclusive Black to Sienna Brown changes **0.0 %** of Cabin Pair pixels. 2. **Driver Hero obstruction:** the camera sat at `[1.45, 1.25, 0.95]`, beside the dashboard. The dashboard (`GEO_Dashboard_Lexus`, bounds x ≤ 0.75, z 0.40–0.96) has a flat untextured end cap, and it filled the left foreground. **Change** - **Driver Hero reframed:** position `[1.9, 1.25, 0.2]`, target `[0.28, 0.76, -0.1]`. The camera now sits rearward and outboard of the dashboard end cap. The FOV stays 38, so the calibrated-FOV contract is unchanged. The values are updated in both `src/config/lexus-camera-presets.ts` and `src/config/vehicles/lexus-rx350-2020.json`. - **Opening view:** `activeCameraView` now defaults to `"hero_driver"`. It is already the first camera tab. **Cabin Pair is unchanged** and still one click away for the dashboard, console, gear selector and cupholders. - **New contract test:** checks that the runtime presets and the vehicle JSON stay in step (position, target, FOV). It failed when only the runtime file was edited and passed once both were updated. - **e2e:** the two `studio-cache-upgrade.spec.ts` assertions about the opening camera now expect Driver Hero. **Objective checks** (local SwiftShader render, 1440×900, canvas only) | Metric | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Opening view pixels changed, Black → Sienna Brown | 0.0 % (Cabin Pair) | 13.2 % (Driver Hero) | | Flat-grey pixels in Driver Hero (mid-luminance, saturation < 14) | 15.5 % | 9.2 % | | Opening camera tab pressed | Cabin Pair | Driver Hero | | Console and page errors | n/a | 0 | The grey metric is a rough heuristic: some seat highlights also count as grey. Use the screenshots as the real evidence. ![Before / after](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..HEwWdao6-J4aVWE2wXVdOva4RfxRnr24JPphmFWlqfo) Visual acceptance stays with the owner's review on the workshop PC (`visual-fidelity-review`); I am not self-certifying it. SwiftShader lighting is not representative of a real GPU. **Clean clone of this branch (Node 22.23.2)** | Step | Result | |---|---| | `npm ci`, typecheck | exit 0 | | lint | exit 0 (0 errors, 4 existing warnings) | | `npm test` | 124/124 passed (+1 new) | | build | exit 0 | **Deferred to the 3D refinement phase (no geometry changed here)** - The dashboard's outboard end cap is a flat untextured face, and a sliver of it is still visible at the left edge of Driver Hero. A door card or A-pillar trim panel in the Blender source would close it properly. - An alternative opening view was tested: a "Front Seats" camera looking rearward over the dashboard at `[0, 1.55, 0.8]`. It shows both seat faces, which suits Duotone, but it adds a fifth camera tab. That is a UI change, so it is left for the redesign proposal. `docs/LEXUS_DEMO_SCOPE_AND_ARCHITECTURE.md` Section 6 keeps the original historical calibration. I have not rewritten it. title: fix(studio): remove Executive Fluted from live composition options
body: ## Summary P0 PR 3 of 5. It removes a composition option the live preview cannot actually show. **Problem:** the assessment found that "Executive Fluted & Armrest Split" rendered pixel-identical to "Bespoke Duotone Bolsters". The specification sheet and the WhatsApp text still listed it as a separate choice, so a customer could pick something the cabin never displayed. **Root cause:** the only thing that reads the tier for rendering is `VisualizationStage`: ```ts secondaryHex = compositionTier === 'bespoke_monotone' ? primaryHex : selectedSecondaryColor.hexCode ``` Duotone and Executive Fluted both took the same branch. No distinct material, mask or geometry path exists for "fluted" or "armrest split". **Change:** - `CompositionTier` changes from `"bespoke_monotone" | "bespoke_duotone" | "executive_fluted"` to `"bespoke_monotone" | "bespoke_duotone"`. - The option is removed from the `compositions` list in `StudioOptions`. - The fallback label lookups in `configurator-context.tsx` (WhatsApp text) and `SummaryBar.tsx` (spec sheet) now handle two tiers. - The matching union in `src/types/configuration.ts` and the line in `README.md` are updated. Because the type itself is narrowed, any leftover `'executive_fluted'` literal now fails `tsc`. No visual effect or geometry was added. The default tier (Duotone) and the Monotone/Duotone behaviour are unchanged. **Verification, clean clone of this branch (Node 22.23.2):** | Step | Result | |---|---| | `npm ci`, typecheck | exit 0 | | lint | exit 0 (0 errors, 18 existing warnings) | | `npm test` | 123/123 passed | | build | exit 0 | **Browser check:** local `next start`, Chromium with SwiftShader. - Composition step lists exactly `Bespoke Monotone`, then `Bespoke Duotone Bolsters` (selected by default). - Specification shows "Bespoke Monotone" with no secondary-accent line. - Specification shows "Bespoke Duotone Bolsters" with the secondary-accent line. - No "Executive Fluted" text anywhere. 0 console or page errors. ![Composition step after](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..Ye-y9PfPPY6JEOV3ifEswroRSRC_QGxCVJk-mdKU6AY) ![Specification, Duotone](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..ebmwfqfHzKTVbKLfu5c5gFBMKbBuGpUUp-alRgJKTK0) The 3D canvas was still loading under SwiftShader in the first screenshot; this PR does not change the cabin rendering. **Follow-up for the 3D refinement phase:** a real fluted-insert or armrest-split composition would need its own material zone or mask in the Blender source before it comes back as an option. title: chore(studio): remove mock auth, /dashboard and /auth scaffolding
body: ## Summary P0 PR 2 of 5. This removes template scaffolding that has no place in the workshop-only Studio. No new auth or backend is added, and WhatsApp stays disabled. **Problem:** the production build shipped `/dashboard`, a generic SaaS template, and `/auth`, a fake sign-in that stored a random user in `localStorage["suyanka_auth_user"]`. `src/app/layout.tsx` also wrapped the whole Studio in that mock `AuthProvider`, although no Studio component used it. **Removed (−1188 lines, 1 line changed):** - `src/app/auth/`, `src/app/dashboard/` - `src/lib/auth/auth-context.tsx`, and `` in `layout.tsx`, which now renders `{children}` directly - `src/components/layout/navbar.tsx` and `footer.tsx`. Nothing imported them, and their only links pointed to `/auth`, `/dashboard` and `/splash`. - `src/components/ui/{badge,button,card,input,tabs}.tsx`, which only the deleted pages and navbar used **Kept on purpose, `/splash`:** it is not template scaffolding. It is the Studio's own branded welcome page, built from `StudioBrand` and `studio.module.css`. The logo on the main page links to it, it has no auth and no 3D canvas, and an existing e2e test covers it as the "approved welcome". I can remove it in a follow-up if the owner prefers. **Verification, clean clone of this branch (Node 22.23.2):** | Step | Result | |---|---| | `npm ci` / typecheck | exit 0 / exit 0 | | lint | exit 0, 0 errors, 4 warnings (was 18; 14 were in deleted files) | | `npm test` | 15 files, 123/123 passed | | `npm run build` | exit 0. Routes are now only `/`, `/_not-found` and `/splash` | Local `next start`: `/` returns 200, `/splash` returns 200, and `/dashboard`, `/auth` and `/auth?mode=signup` return 404. In Chromium with SwiftShader, `/` renders one live canvas with the heading "Make it personal.". Console and page errors are 0, and `localStorage` has no keys. The logo → `/splash` → "Create your interior" → `/` round trip works. ![Studio after removal](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..75g5kqjJXEfRaOhjfwQ52ST4dy01q02v0XcCSlApFS4) **Left for later (outside this PR):** - `src/lib/utils.ts` (`cn`, `formatDate`) and `src/lib/db/` (Drizzle and Supabase client/schema) have no importers. - Their packages (`clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, db clients) remain in `package.json`. I left these alone to keep this PR to the routes and the auth dependency, and they can go in a small dependency-cleanup PR. title: test: make Lexus CLI gate tests generate their own synthetic fixtures
body: ## Summary P0 PR 1 of 5 from the 2026-11-11 independent assessment. It makes `npm test` pass from a clean clone, which should turn the `Quality gates` workflow green again. That workflow has failed on `main` since 22 Oct. **Problem:** two tests in `tests/lexus-gate.test.ts` failed with `expected 1 to be +0` on CI and on every fresh checkout: - `passes CLI validation on the synthetic Lexus GLB with exit code 0` - `passes CLI validation on the synthetic Lexus L2A prototype GLB with exit code 0` **Root cause:** the tests launched `scripts/validate-glb.mjs --asset tests/fixtures/*.glb`. `tests/fixtures/*.glb` is gitignored, and only the separate `validate:lexus:fixture` and `validate:lexus:l2a` scripts create those files. The validator hit `ENOENT` and exited 1. The earlier "all pass" reports came from local trees that already had the generated files. **Change (test file only):** each test now creates its own Draco fixture in a temporary directory it already owns, then validates that file: ```ts const asset = join(temp, "fixture.glb"); writeFileSync(asset, await createLexusSyntheticFixture({ draco: true })); // L2A: createLexusPrototypeFixture spawnSync(node, ["scripts/validate-glb.mjs", "--scope", "lexus", "--synthetic", "--asset", asset, ...]); ``` The bytes match what the `validate:lexus:*` scripts write, since both use the same `make-fixture.mjs` export with `--draco`. No assertion was loosened, and no application, asset or Blender files changed. **Clean-clone verification:** fresh `git clone` of this branch, with no `tests/fixtures/` directory, on Node 22.23.2: | Step | Result | |---|---| | `npm ci` | exit 0 | | `npm run typecheck` | exit 0 | | `npm run lint` | exit 0 (0 errors, 18 existing warnings) | | `npm run test` | exit 0: 15 files, 123/123 tests passed (was 2 failed / 121 passed) | | `npm run build` | exit 0 | **Not covered here:** - 3 Python test errors that depend on gitignored Blender output. These will be documented in PR 5. - `next build` rewrites the tracked `next-env.d.ts` (`.next/dev/types` → `.next/types`). This already happened before this PR and is left alone.
